chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"(1 ) Changing to a mandatory “Actual \nProduction History” (APH) basis by \nremoving the Premium Adjustment \nTable and providing for cancellation for \nnot furnishing records; (2) adding as a \ncause of loss the unavoidable failure of \nirrigation water supply; (3) changing the \nmethod of computing indemnities when \nacreage, share or practice is \nunderreported; (4) changing the \ndefinition of unit to encompass the \nentire ASCS farm serial number; and (5) \ndeleting Appendix A. The intended \neffect of this rule is to comply with the \nprovisions of Department Regulation \n1512-1 requiring review of regulations \nissued by FCIC for need, currency, \nclarity, and effectiveness. The authority \nfor the promulgation of this rule is \ncontained in the Federal Crop Insurance \nAct, as amended.\ne f f e c t iv e d a t e: December 31,1984.\nFOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT.  \nPeter F. Cole, Secretary, Federal Crop \nInsurance Corporation, U.S. Department \nof Agriculture, Washington, D.C., 20250, \ntelephone (202) 447-3325.\nSUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: This \naction has been reviewed under USDA \n.^procedures established by Departmental \nRegulation No. 1512-1 (December 15, \n1983). This action constitutes a review \nas to the need, currency, clarity, and \neffectiveness of these regulations under \nthose procedures. The sunset review \ndate established for these regulations is \nAugust 30,1989.\nMerritt W. Sprague, Manager, FCIC, \nhas determined that this action (1) is not \na major rule as defined by Executive\nOrder No. 12291 (February 17,1981), \nbecause it will not result in: (a) An \nannual effect on the economy of $100 \nmillion or more; (b) major increases in \ncosts or prices for consumers, individual \nindustries, Federal, State, or local \ngovernments, or a geographical region; \nor (c) significant adverse effects on \ncompetition, employment, investment, \nproductivity, innovation, or the ability of \nU.S.-based enterprises to compete with \nforeign-based enterprises in domestic or \nexport markets; and (2) will not increase \nthe Federal paperwork burden for \nindividuals, small businesses, and other \npersons.\nThe title and number of the Federal \nAssistance Program to which this \nproposed rule apply are: Title—Crop \nInsurance; Number 10.450.\nThis program is not subject to the \nprovisions of Executive Order 12372 \nwhich requires intergovernmental \nconsultation with State and local \nofficials. See the Notice related to 7 CFR \nPart 3015, Subpart V, published at 48 FR \n29115 (June 24,1983).\nThis action is exempt from t(ie \nprovisions of the Regulatory Flexibility \nAct; therefore, no Regulatory Flexibility \nAnalysis was prepared.\nThis action is not expected to have \nany significant impact on the quality of \nthe human environment, health, and \nsafety. Therefore, neither an \nEnvironmental Assessment nor an \nEnvironmental Impact Statement is \nneeded.\nOn Monday, November 28,1984, FCIC \npublished a notice of proposed \nrulemaking in the Federal Register at 49 \nFR 46395, revising and reissuing the \nPotato Crop Insurance Regulations (7 \nCFR Part 422), effective for the 1985 and \nsucceeding crop years. The public was \ngiven 30 days in which to submit written \ncomments on the proposed rule.\nComments were received contending \nthat the Actual Production History \n(APH) program constitutes a \n“mandatory Individual Yield Coverage \n(IYC)” program and is therefore illegal \nunder the terms of the Crop Insurance \nAct, which required a pilot IYC program. \nFCIC rejects that contention.\nThe APH and IYC programs are quite \ndifferent, although they share common \ngoals. For example: IYC is an optional \nprogram; APH is not; IYC is available on \na small number of crops; APH will \neventually be offered on all insurable \ncrops; Under IYC, coverage levels are \nadjusted at fixed rates; under APH, both \ncoverages and rates are adjusted; Under \nIYC, a premium adjustment table is \nintended to individualize rates; under \nAPH, the premium adjustment table is \nnot necessary because the rates are\nalready individualized under the yield \nspan-rating concept.\nIt is further clear from the statutory \nlanguage, that although a pilot IYC \nprogram is required, a broad IYC \nprogram mandatory in nature is not \nprohibited.\nComments were also received \ncontending that APH should be \nabandoned or postponed because the \nAPH concept will lead to declining \nsales. The evidence does not support \nthis contention.\nIn the only two crops currently being \noperated under the APH concept— \ncotton and rice—producer participation \nis up substantially over previous year \nlevels. Considering the relative \nincompatibility of cotton and rice to the \nAPH concept in that yield levels have \nbeen steadily declining, the increase in \nparticipation is even more telling. If \nanything, APH will encourage more \nfarmers to consider crop insurance as a \nrisk transfer program that ever before.\nSince policy changes must, by \ncontract, be on file by December 31,\n1984, good cause is shown for making \nthis rule effective immediately.\nOther than minor changes in language \nand format, the principal changes in the \npotato policy and in the certified seed \npotato option amendment are:","sections_touched":["Part 3015","Part 422"],"signing_date":"1984-12-21","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"filing_date":null,"grade":"held_text_lead","instrument_id":"EO:12495","page_or_item":"49 FR 50153, PDF pages 9-9; FR-1984-12-27.pdf PDF pages 1-40 of 226","requires_page_check":false,"sha256":"0c260b96585e062c8d1fcbc4435ad46eaa3f6ff05cd980c870f9ce5829cb8b0e","signing_date":"1984-12-21","text_path":"jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_12495_49_FR_50153_PDF_pages_9-9_5f77b08f6a.txt","text_sha256":"76d752e8acb6e9d955a6b88234746006a727660a6de80db0651a282814711b11","url":"https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-1984-12-27/pdf/FR-1984-12-27.pdf"},"verb":"transfer"}],"generic_refs_excluded":241,"id":"CHAIN:EO:12372","notes":"Named, located change provisions only; missing provisions and unheld texts remain dossier gaps. Undated events sort last.","target_id":"EO:12372"}

12549 (Reagan, signed 1986-02-18, 51 FR 6370, published 1986-02-21) establishes a government-wide system of debarment and suspension for nonprocurement programs: executive departments and agencies shall participate in the system and a debarment or suspension by one agency has government-wide effect (section 1(a)), the activities covered (section 1(b)) and the programs not covered, including procurement (section 1(c)); agencies shall follow government-wide criteria and minimum due process procedures (section 2(a)), report debarred and suspended participants (section 2(b)) and not allow a party excluded by any agency to participate except by written exception (section 2(c)); agencies shall issue implementing regulations consistent with OMB guidelines, with deadlines of four and twelve months from the guidelines (section 3); the Interagency Committee on Debarment and Suspension is constituted (section 4); OMB designates an agency to keep the exclusion list and chair the committee, with a first report due within two years (section 5); OMB may issue guidelines (section 6); and OMB reports to the President within three years (section 7). The dossier inventory numbered the clauses incorrectly (the section 2(c) text was labelled section 5, and section 3 and parts of sections 5 to 7 were mislabelled or merged), so the inventory is corrected with overrides to twelve scopes, one per paragraph or section, covering every operative part of the held text after the preamble. The held current sources show the order in effect: a note in the U.S. Code under 31 U.S.C. 6101 prints it and a statute enacted in 2008 and amended in 2011 and 2013 identifies the committee by reference to sections 4 and 5 of the order, and 2 CFR 180.110 in the eCFR as of 2026-10-14 still refers to exclusions under the order. EO 12689 (1989), which the Federal Register note lists as a cross-reference, extends government-wide effect of debarment to procurement and expressly refers to nonprocurement activities covered by EO 12549; it recites EO 12549 and does not amend or revoke it. EO 13904 (2020) also only recites EO 12549 as policy. The order cites no statute as authority (the Constitution and laws of the United States), so no authority statute needs checking. The deadlines in sections 3, 5 and 7 are deadlines, not ends; no held source dates performance of those one-time steps, so no end is recorded for them.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"No earlier end: no section states a term or condition, and the later orders that name EO 12549 (EO 12689 and EO 13904) only recite or build on it; no held source shows a later general rule extinguishing any command in it. Deadlines in sections 3, 5 and 7 are not ends.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The participation duty, the covered-activities and exclusions text, the three duties in section 2, the regulation-issuing duty, the committee, the list and designation duty, the guidelines authority and the reporting duty are independent; none depends on another for its continuation.\",\"savings_check\":\"No ending event, so no savings question arises; regulations issued under section 3 and guidelines under section 6 continue to stand in the CFR.\",\"scope_check\":\"Twelve scopes: sections 1(a), 1(b), 1(c), 2(a), 2(b), 2(c), 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7. Section 2 is split because its lead-in and paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) command different things. The preamble states purposes and commands nothing.\"}","review_dependency_issues":[],"reviews":[{"file_sha256":"68c1aa0a62856a1af78c2b7a12d63aa64f52d9373a83f8b9eba05eb51e415931","path":"research/excavator/claude-papinian-2026-11-10/y11/packet/complete-v1/receipts/research/excavator/claude-papinian-2026-11-10/y11/packet/reviews/BLIND_REVIEW_A.jsonl","pointer":"line:2","review_kind":"independent_ai_source_review","scope":"whole_case","verdict":"rejected","version_binding":"exact"},{"file_sha256":"ee30565085d210f17eb367bacda2ab1e7cde67d19590bd5f2bb8109b1b1a374e","path":"research/excavator/claude-papinian-2026-11-10/y11/packet/complete-v1/receipts/research/excavator/claude-papinian-2026-11-10/y11/packet/reviews/BLIND_REVIEW_B.jsonl","pointer":"line:4","review_kind":"independent_ai_source_review","scope":"whole_case","verdict":"rejected","version_binding":"exact"},{"file_sha256":"68c1aa0a62856a1af78c2b7a12d63aa64f52d9373a83f8b9eba05eb51e415931","path":"research/excavator/claude-papinian-2026-11-10/y11/packet/reviews/BLIND_REVIEW_A.jsonl","pointer":"line:2","review_kind":"independent_ai_source_review","scope":"whole_case","verdict":"rejected","version_binding":"exact"},{"file_sha256":"ee30565085d210f17eb367bacda2ab1e7cde67d19590bd5f2bb8109b1b1a374e","path":"research/excavator/claude-papinian-2026-11-10/y11/packet/reviews/BLIND_REVIEW_B.jsonl","pointer":"line:4","review_kind":"independent_ai_source_review","scope":"whole_case","verdict":"rejected","version_binding":"exact"}],"scopes":[{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:12549#sec1"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":["state_at_cutoff","current_predicate","later_events"],"scope_id":"EO:12549#corrected-sec1a"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:12549#sec1-b"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":["state_at_cutoff","current_predicate","later_events"],"scope_id":"EO:12549#corrected-sec1b"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:12549#sec1-c"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":["state_at_cutoff","cur - **ACT:EO:12591>EO:12618**; S837b75f14883c0e0a13121a4; {"actor_id":"EO:12618","char_end":2182,"char_start":594,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":2182,"char_start":594,"text":"Title 3— Executive Order 12618 of December 22, 1987\nUniform Treatment of Federally Funded InventionsThe President\nBy the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the \nUnited States of America, and having concluded that the ability of the United \nStates to achieve the statutorily prescribed policy (35 U.S.C. 200) of using the \npatent system to promote the utilization of inventions arising from federally \nsupported research or development requires that Federal agencies follow \nuniform policies in administering patents and licenses conceived or first \nreduced to practice during the course of federally funded research, Executive \nOrder No. 12591 of April 10,1987, is amended by redesignating Sections 1(b)(5) \nand (6) as 1(b)(6) and (7), respectively, and by adding a new Section 1(b)(5) as\n‘(5) administer all patents and licenses to inventions made with federal \nassistance, which are owned by the non-profit contractor or grantee, in \naccordance with Section 202(c)(7) of Title 35 of the United States Code as \namended by Public Law 98-620, without regard to limitations on licensing \nfound in that section prior to amendment or in Institutional Patent Agreements \nnow in effect that were entered into before that law was enacted on Novem­\nber 8,1984, unless, in the case of an invention that has not been marketed, the \nfunding agency determines, based on information in its files, that the contrac­\ntor or grantee has not taken adequate steps to market the inventions, in \naccordance with applicable law or an Institutional Patent Agreement;”.\nfollows:"}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12591>EO:12618","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. ## Valla review leads and component attestations

Review lead only. Every case needs separate applicability, earlier-ending, scope, independent-command, savings and independent whole-case review.
Preparation attestations never approve legal conclusions or replace whole-case review.
